questions.prompt: What does OpenAI's evaluation guide call "it seems like it's working" as a test?

options.text: A vibe-based eval, which it lists as an anti-pattern.
options.explanation: Right. The guide also warns against waiting until you ship before you test.

options.text: A good first step for a pilot, before any numbers are used.
options.explanation: The guide lists it as an anti-pattern. Agree numbers before the pilot starts.

options.text: Continuous evaluation, run after every change.
options.explanation: Continuous evaluation means running real tests on every change, not a feeling.

questions.prompt: Which test cases should a pilot include, according to OpenAI's evaluation guide?

options.text: Only typical cases, so the results look stable.
options.explanation: The guide asks for more than typical cases. A test set without hard cases hides problems.

options.text: Only the hardest cases, so nothing can surprise you.
options.explanation: The guide wants a mix. Only hard cases wouldn't show how the system does on normal work.
Right. Anthropic's guide also says to include edge cases and mirror the real mix of tasks.

questions.prompt: When should you agree the go, change or stop rule for a pilot?

options.text: At the end, once everyone has seen the results.
options.explanation: Then the rule bends to fit the result. Agree it before day one.
Right. Criteria and the decision rule come first, so the result decides, not opinions.
